claims.statement: IDC forecasts about 1.15 billion active agents and 217 billion agent actions per day in 2029. Agent/action counts are not measurements of CPU seconds or physical sockets.
McKinsey's 2026 survey reports 40% of large-enterprise respondents (>USD1B annual revenues) vs 22% of smaller-organization respondents say their organizations are scaling AI agents.
Gartner forecasts more than 40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end 2027, based on perceived cost/value/risk challenges.
AMD argues that agentic workflows may require standalone CPU-centric execution racks, separately from GPU-host CPUs; AMD's May 2026 >USD120B 2030 TAM is a management forecast.

scenarios.hypothesis: At an illustrative fixed IDC 2029 action forecast, assumed per-action CPU time changes gross provisioned socket equivalents by orders of magnitude.

outputs.caution: Not incremental units, annual shipments or revenue. Excludes idle RAM, placement, backend duplicates, spare fleets and CPU-GPU host splitting.

signals.actor: AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud
signals.statement: Vendor-described agent sandbox architectures range from long-running per-session microVMs to isolated dynamic sessions and in-instance shared sandboxes.
signals.inference: Agent/server conversion depends on RAM reservations, CPU duty cycle and pooling, not count of logical agents alone.

signals.statement: IDC population/activity forecasts, McKinsey surveyed enterprise scaling and Gartner cancellation forecasts have different universes and do not provide observed chip purchases.
signals.inference: Need workflow-denominator, attrition and buyer-specific execution bridges before adopting market figures.

hypotheses.thesis: For persistent personal and enterprise agents, memory and isolation reservations can drive physical sockets even with low CPU duty cycles.
hypotheses.alternative: MicroVM/session pooling greatly reduces idle resource reservations.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Benchmark dedicated microVM, prewarmed-pool and shared-instance RAM GiB-hours/concurrent sessions per physical host at matched successful tasks.

hypotheses.thesis: Code-build-test agents may require far higher physical CPU core-seconds per successful task than lightweight consumer agent actions.
hypotheses.alternative: Most agent actions are API/I/O bound or use already provisioned CI/cloud fleets.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Trace matched successful end-to-end coding, browser, data and business tasks at physical host CPU counters including retries.

hypotheses.thesis: Local agent model inference can reduce cloud core-seconds per task but simultaneously generate new backend workflows.
hypotheses.alternative: Tasks migrate almost entirely to endpoints; net cloud load falls.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Per-step execution location trace and controlled price elasticity test with source and destination CPU fleet impacts.

hypotheses.thesis: Agentic global CPU demand may rise without an equally large x86 socket opportunity because Arm/custom ISA and physical core density capture capacity.
hypotheses.alternative: x86 compatibility/TCO retains most installed agent execution.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Measure buyer×workload physical ISA and actual shipment mix/ASP, not total cloud instance revenue.

questions.method: Controlled replay benchmark with task success criteria and physical host counters across ISA/runtime, initial 20+ trials per case.

questions.question: How many idle and active GiB-hours and concurrent isolation slots must be provisioned per agent session by runtime architecture?
questions.method: Benchmark active/idle reserved RAM, CPU, concurrent sessions and peak host placement at homogeneous hosts.
questions.decision_impacted: Memory versus CPU constrained fleet size

questions.question: Which CPU-side execution events happen on endpoints, cloud, private enterprise and remote SaaS during each hybrid workflow?
questions.method: Per-step transition matrix with actual cloud backend resource consumption and demand elasticity.
questions.decision_impacted: Net placement and 2030 CPU fleet; extends D002

questions.question: What incremental agent work requires new physical hardware rather than spare/displaced CPU capacity or a replacement fleet refresh?
questions.method: Reconcile buyer physical stock, deployed sockets, usable spare, host memory and actual annual shipments.
questions.decision_impacted: Incremental CPU silicon revenue; extends D007/D008

questions.question: What are AMD/Intel/Arm/custom CPU hardware shares and net ASP by the economic buyer and the actual workload?
questions.method: Buyer-by-workload physical BOM/source matched to ISA, unit shipments and realized ASP not list prices.

questions.question: How are IDC action counts, Microsoft/AWS sandbox sessions and completed workflows related without double-counting?
questions.method: Crosswalk stable workflow/session/action/execution IDs with concurrency and retry taxonomy.

methods.name: Workflow-purpose and constrained CPU+memory capacity bridge
methods.procedure: Uniquely attribute successful initiating workflows to one primary purpose; assign distinct execution steps to runtime/site/physical host; measure attempts, CPU core-seconds, peak RAM and idle session reservation; determine homogeneous host pool binding CPU/RAM/I/O/isolation capacity; subtract usable spare and displaced capacity; reconcile installed socket stock and yearly replacement/new shipments; estimate CPU silicon dollars as net realized chip ASP times physical shipments, allocated once by buyer×ISA×procurement channel.
assumptions: A consumer/enterprise purpose partition is not the same axis as hardware buyer, industry or cloud provider.
Physical hardware host event IDs prevent double-counted nested delegations.
Idle/resident RAM matters independently of CPU duty cycles.
No assumed interchangeability between in-house enterprise, endpoint and cloud spare pools.
No new socket sale until capacity exceeds existing usable fleet; replacement still counts as annual shipment.
Scenarios must never become observed hardware-market metrics without verified source/denominator.

requirements.outcome: Integrate agent purpose, workflow telemetry, runtime placement and immutable demand-model runs into existing evidence-first SQLite planning; design only.
acceptance_criteria: agent_demand_segment: exactly one primary purpose per initiating workflow plus optional secondary tags
agent_workflow_profile: versioned steps, successful outputs, attempts, core-seconds and GiB-hours
runtime_placement_profile: site, architecture, isolation topology, peak concurrency and idle reservation
segment_demand_projection: dated scenario, stock flow, buyer/channel/ISA and evidence pointers
Keep legacy T001-T009 and existing buyer ledger authoritative; distinguish synthetic vs measured

promotions.decision_note: AMD >USD120B 2030 management forecast already stored as T002; historical vintage remains unchanged.
Existing IDC whole-system spending reference; not CPU chip TAM.
Demand adoption driver—not a CPU silicon TAM forecast; separate future schema/metric after review.
Survey calibration needs explicit response universe, subgroup sample and methodology review; do not backfill worldwide population.
Detailed method is linked analytical guidance, not an observed market measurement.

handoff.summary: Eight primary public sources, eight checked original assertions, two survey respondent-share observations, three distinct non-CPU silicon forecasts, one transparent synthetic stress test, hypotheses, requirements, and six measurement questions; no changes to canonical CPU TAM forecast table.
changed_decisions: Agent demand classified by primary purpose independently of physical buyer/industry/channel.
Physical CPU capacity model requires binding RAM, I/O, peak concurrency/isolation as well as active CPU core-hours.
IDC agent actions are useful adoption drivers but cannot imply CPU shipments without measured host utilization, placement and spare capacity.
next_actions: Instrument completed task CPU core-seconds by D001 across coding/browser/business workload types.
Measure active+idle RAM GiB-hours per concurrent AWS/Azure/GCP-style runtime topology.
Survey denominator and production conversion checks before extrapolation.
Reconcile projected net physical sockets, ISA and CPU-only ASP by actual end buyer; preserve scenario vintages.
limits: No host-level CPU benchmark or measured socket fleet data was gathered.
Vendor documentation describes product design, not independent performance measurements.
IDC/Gartner data are forecasts and McKinsey percentages are respondent subsets, not a census.
No new public AMD 2030 management TAM row; existing T002/T006/T008 and T009 retained.
Public, link-and-extract sources only; no confidential former-employer/client material.
